- For named fields: `wrap = '(?P<name>%s)'` so we get `(?P<name><regex>)`

The `s` is the regex pattern for the field. If `s` contains internal groups (parentheses), those become additional capture groups within the outer group.

For example, if `s = r'\d+\.\d+'`, then `wrap % s` gives `( \d+\.\d+ )`.
If `s = r'(\d+\.\d*)'`, then `wrap % s` gives `( (\d+\.\d*) )`.

The first inner group becomes a nested group inside the outer group. This means when we call `.group(n)`, we get different results.
